subject: Re: Multiple trial credit requests / escalation for SupplyChain.ai
messages:
From: Evan Torres <evan@sc-ai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting another trial top-up for SupplyChain.ai

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the pilot credits you provided last month — the team ran a handful of production prompts and we saw encouraging results. We're ramping a second pilot across a new internal group and would like to request another 50k eval credits to keep the tests running for two more weeks.

I realize we've already had a top-up request in July and an extension in August; this new group is separate and will be used by our procurement/ops team. If easier, I'm happy to sign a short addendum or provide additional company verifications. Procurement's contact is procurement@sc-ai.com.

Attached is a short video and a few screenshots of the integration. Appreciate quick help — demo in the next 10 days would help us move to a paid proof-of-concept.

Best,
Evan Torres
Head of AI Partnerships
SupplyChain.ai

Attachments: sc-ai_demo.mp4 (referenced), integration-screen-1.png
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Torres <evan@sc-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Requesting another trial top-up for SupplyChain.ai

Evan —

Thanks for the note and the screenshots. Happy to help when it's a clear POC path. I pulled a quick summary of your previous credits: SupplyChain.ai had a July top-up (25k) and an August extension (15k). Before we approve another 50k, two quick asks so the team can greenlight: 

- Can you confirm these are the same legal entity and billing domain (supplychain.ai) — we need confirmation to avoid multi-account crediting.
- Please provide the names and corporate emails for the new group (so we can scope seats vs. multiple accounts).
- If you can share a short mutual action plan or expected milestones for the next 14 days that would be ideal.

I need to loop in Ops for a brief compliance check — cc'ing Marissa and Ben. If you can return the two bullets above today, we should be able to move quickly.

Aditya
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: FWD: SupplyChain.ai — repeated trial/top-up request — needs fraud review

Marissa / Ben / Steph —

Forwarding a new request from SupplyChain.ai (Evan Torres). They've already had two recent credit events and are asking for another 50k. Evan says it's a different internal group, but I want Ops + Trust to validate before we approve more credits.

Attached I pulled our credit events log for this account (trial-requests-log.csv) and a set of screenshots Evan sent. Quick notes from my side:
- July 14: 25k credits issued (account: sales@supplychain.ai)
- Aug 22: 15k extension/approval (same org but different contact emails included)
- Sep 30: short burst of high-volume eval usage from a range of IPs (see attached)

Can someone run the following checks:
1) Confirm all emails are MX/DMARC-aligned with supplychain.ai and whether we see multiple accounts owning the same org.
2) Check for velocity/automation signals (scripted signups, rapid API key creation, multiple trial IDs).
3) If we deny, what is the appropriate remediation messaging and whether we offer a paid pilot discount instead.

Evan is asking for a near-immediate decision; he says procurement needs credits to demo next week. I'm inclined to pause until we confirm, but open to exceptions if there's a signed comms or PO.

Thanks —Aditya

Attachments: trial-requests-log.csv, sc-ai_screenshots.zip
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Torres <evan@sc-ai.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FWD: SupplyChain.ai — repeated trial/top-up request — needs fraud review

Team —

Quick summary after a short review: 
- MX/DMARC: supplychain.ai is properly configured. No immediate domain spoofing.
- Accounts: We found three related trial accounts that map to SupplyChain.ai contacts across different email aliases. Two accounts were created within 48 hours of each other in July and show similar usage patterns.
- Velocity: There's a short burst on Sep 30 coming from three distinct AWS IP ranges; we see repeated API key rotations that suggest script-driven activity.

Recommendation: Deny the ad-hoc 50k credit request for now. Offer a structured paid pilot (30-day, capped tokens at reduced rate) under a simple PO or an MSA addendum. If they supply company legal confirmation and the names/emails for the new group we can consider limited credits (max 10k) post-contract.

Suggested messaging to Evan (short):
"Thanks Evan — we reviewed activity and saw multiple related trial accounts and scripted key rotations. To protect both parties we can't approve a further ad-hoc top-up. We'd love to run a paid 30-day pilot; we can offer a 25% credit on the pilot fee if you sign a PO by Oct 15. If you can send corporate verification and a list of the new users, we can discuss a limited 10k credit while the PO is processed."

Please let me know if you want me to send the note. Also attaching SOC2-request.pdf that Evan included in a later message — procurement asked for it but we'll redact internal notes.

Marissa Cole
Senior Ops Manager — Redwood Inference
